question: I'm an IS sophomore (P-013) on academic warning. Given my AW unit restrictions, can I realistically still graduate in 4 years (Spring 2028)?

domain_contributions.programs: P-013 has completed limited IS requirements (67-100, 67-250, 67-262, 15-121, 21-127, etc.) — still needs 67-272, 67-373, concentration courses, electives
domain_contributions.schedules: 67-272 offered Spring 2026 ✓; 67-373 offered Spring 2026 ✓ (but not yet eligible); future semesters need planning
domain_contributions.policies: AW: no overload, so each semester limited to ~45 units. If AW persists multiple semesters, fewer courses per semester, potentially delaying graduation

key_facts: P-013 has ~2.5 years remaining to Spring 2028 target (sophomore now)
AW limits each semester to ~3-4 standard courses
P-013 needs: 67-272 (Spring 2026), then 67-373 (earliest: semester after 67-272), plus IS concentration and electives
If AW is resolved this semester, P-013 can resume normal or overloaded semesters
4-year graduation is feasible if AW is resolved promptly and course sequence is optimized
If AW persists through multiple semesters, graduation may slip by 1 semester
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing program requirements lists many remaining courses but cannot account for the per-semester unit cap imposed by AW. Knowing only the policy gives the unit cap but cannot project how many semesters the remaining program requires.
common_mistake: Assuming AW permanently derails graduation; or conversely, assuming 4-year graduation is straightforward without accounting for the per-semester load cap
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs): Count remaining IS requirements — likely 15+ courses remaining
Step 2 (policies): AW cap = ~3-4 courses/semester; ~5 semesters remaining to Spring 2028
Step 3 (schedules): Verify key IS courses (67-272, 67-373) are offered in the right semesters
Conclusion: 4-year graduation is feasible if AW is resolved within 1-2 semesters; risky if AW continues through junior year
